title: Actual-ring finite coefficient transport and normalized local restriction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with an algebra embedding $i:E\to F$, and their actual valuation rings $A,B$ and uniformizers from [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For schemes $T$ in universe $u$ take $E,F$ in universe $u+1$, with the actual-ring adic data and completed coefficient sheaves $R_T,S_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use the integer inclusion and quotient inclusions of [def-weil-pbc-integer-quotient-inclusions]. In the adic-ideal-power presentations, define $q_n:A/I_A^{n+1}\to B/I_B^{n+1}$ by the quotient lift of that same integer inclusion. Define $c_T:R_T\to S_T$ to be the unique map with $c_T;\pi_{B,n}=\pi_{A,n};(q_n)_T$ for every $n\geq0$, using the coefficient sheaf maps of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Its naturality for $g:X\to Y$ is $c_Y;a_B=a_A;g_*c_X$, where $a_A,a_B$ are the canonical completed structure maps. Define the ambient scalar functor to be the existing derived change of rings along $c_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Define its scalar/restriction comparison to be [def-weil-pbc-normalized-scalar-restriction] specialized to this natural square, retaining both its ordinary adjunction normalization and its cochain K-flat normalization. All coefficient rings, quotient indices and structure maps are the specified ones; no arbitrary ring map or natural isomorphism is selected.

source.place: Exactness clause: actual integral completed coefficient extension and its pullback compatibility; quotient normalization and Stacks 03EL/0D6D.

proof.text: The ideal of pbcPadicCoefficientDatum is the span of the recorded uniformizer. Apply integralScalar_quotient_kernel of [def-weil-pbc-integer-quotient-inclusions] directly; its ideal-power presentation is definitionally the same. This proves the quotient lift well-defined for every positive exponent, without an unramifiedness assumption.

Postcomposition of finite continuous-function presheaves respects composition by extensionality, and sheafification preserves this equality. Quotient induction shows that the finite quotient inclusions commute with consecutive reduction. NatTrans.ofOpSequence supplies the map of the strict coefficient systems of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Apply Mathlib lim.map, limMap_π and limit.hom_ext to obtain existence, the prescribed projection equations, and uniqueness of the completed coefficient map.

The constant-section formula defining pbcLevelConstantComparison in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], together with sheafify_hom_ext, identifies its hom with AdicCoefficients.constantComparison. Functoriality of sheafification then shows that this comparison commutes with every finite quotient ring homomorphism. Combine this square and its inverse with proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap_naturality from [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to prove naturality of completedFiniteCoefficientMap in the finite quotient coefficients.

Apply every target limit projection to the inverse-image coefficient square for [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Its defining limit.lift equations, the completed coefficient map projection equations, and the finite-level naturality just proved identify both composites. limit.hom_ext gives the completed square. Naturality of the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction unit transports it to the direct-image square, and forgetting commutativity gives exactly the specified ring-sheaf equation. The scalar functor and normalized restriction comparison remain the recorded specializations of [def-weil-pbc-normalized-scalar-restriction].
